title: Record the teardown-leak route, its loader key, the four states the pane renders and the two absences it states as their own lines

The entry cost the list no line, because this task folded the M047 `components` note’s three lines into one: `visual-qa`, `tutor-foundations`, `tutor-signals`, `tutor-routing`, `webmcp-rehearsal`, `webmcp`, `components`, `copy-check`, `interaction-story`, `dead-click`, `what-changed`, the `appRoutes` declaration (line 113) and the mapped literal’s `loadComponent` (146) and `data` (147) all kept their numbers. The route registers nothing and measures nothing: it reaches the pane that renders the join’s answer.

loader.statement: the `teardown-leak` key is one entry of the `LOADERS` map and it is the only path to `panel-teardown-leak.ts`: the demo looks the key up by the name the route’s `data.surface` states, awaits the dynamic import, calls the module’s default export with the sample fact, and sets the state and the lines the module answers. The key cost one line, and that line is paid for by folding one line of the `fields` fact’s comment into its neighbour rather than by adding a line — the loader resolution block (717, 723–726), the component template (671–687) and every earlier fact keep their numbers, so the surface records which pin this file’s lines re-resolve at this head. The fact is the join’s own answer over the console record and the shipped digest: `state: finding`, `code: NG0205`, the body the installed build prints, `owner: null`, both absences, six claims each carrying its artefact path and the sequence `release-then-diagnostic` — and `panel-demo.spec.ts` rebuilds that record from the shipped record and digest, evaluates the shipped join from its committed text and holds this fact to that answer field for field.

answer.statement: the join answers `{ state, code, message, owner, absences, claims, detail }` with every field in every state. The demo’s sample is the `finding` answer: the code the message’s own body carries, the body with the stack frames dropped, no owner (no field of the message names one), `owner-not-in-the-message` beside `handle-record-not-held`, one claim per statement with the record or digest path that states it, and the join’s own detail sentence. T001 measured that the diagnostic is not producible on either driven target (`research/raw/m059-record-shapes.json` `producible`: 0 NG0205 over 38 portal console lines and 4 fixture lines), so this record states the sample’s record as one written in the measured shape from the measured printed string rather than one captured on a page.

No browser was opened, no page was read, no profiler was tapped and no build was run.

No page read produced this answer and none could: T001 measured 0 NG0205 across 38 portal console lines and 4 fixture console lines over six navigations, so the diagnostic has never been captured on a page. The sample record is written in the measured shape from the measured printed string (`digest.printedByTheInstalledBuild.printedAs`) and its two `order` values are sample positions — the message’s and the one release record’s — not measurements. The milestone ships the absence-only answer and records that as its finding (PLAN R1).

The record does not measure what the pane looks like. The six sentences it renders are enumerated in `panel-teardown-leak.ts`’s `PANE_SENTENCES` and carry one row each in `extension/copy-digest.json` under the surface `teardown-leak`; this record names the states and the field each reads rather than reproducing the rendering.

The record does not claim the copy record was re-measured by this task’s first pass alone. `research/raw/m048-surface-copy.json` stated 29 surfaces and 206 sentences and did not carry `panel-teardown-leak.ts`; the plan was then repaired to add that record to this task’s `files:`, and the same task re-measured it over the thirtieth surface — its six registry sentences with the keys and texts the digest already carries, its eleven label constants (`LABELS`) and its one inline label — so that record now states 30 surfaces and 212 sentences, `scripts/copy-check.test.mjs` is green at 30 of 30, and the `copyRecordSurfaces` and `copyRecordSentencesCompared` counts below are the re-measured record’s (see `openDependency`).

verdict: measured: the panel route `teardown-leak` is one lazy route — a `PANEL_SURFACES` entry spread into `appRoutes` by the one mapped literal, costing the list no line because this task folded the M047 note’s three lines into one — whose `data.surface` names the `teardown-leak` key of `panel-demo.ts`’s `LOADERS`, and that key is the only path to `panel-teardown-leak.ts`. The pane renders the join’s four states and nothing it did not state: `finding` names the code and the body and the owner only where a field of the message names one, never the stack, the capture’s `component`, the last component mounted or the arrival order; `absent` names the code searched for and the count read and never a clean bill of health; `cannot-tell` names the reason the answer’s own claim states; `empty` states that no record was read. `owner-not-in-the-message` and `handle-record-not-held` render as two groups of lines, each with its own state word, sentence and detail, never folded. The pane names no cause — the sequence claim states `release-then-diagnostic` as the release and the diagnostic and not as a reason — and it names no subscription, effect, timer, handle, fix, remedy or schematic, because the answer carries none. The panel carries 29 surfaces and 29 loader keys, the route table 38 ordered paths, and `extension/copy-digest.json` 204 rows, six of them this pane’s sentences.
